blocking: reverts the SEC-68 local hub auth hardening; disables hub auth by default
security_notes: This is a security regression, not a fix. `createHubAuthToken()` in sdk/packages/core/src/hub/discovery/index.ts is changed from `randomBytes(32).toString("hex")` to returning `""` unless `CLINE_HUB_AUTH_TOKEN` is set, and `isValidHubAuthToken()` in hub/server/hub-websocket-server.ts is relaxed so an empty expected token accepts an empty candidate. Net effect: by default the local hub WebSocket daemon (which drives agent sessions and therefore shell execution) accepts unauthenticated connections from any local process. This directly reverts commit f597bd031 'feat: Secure local hub daemon with discovery auth token SEC-68 (#298)'. The 0600 discovery file is the only remaining barrier and it becomes irrelevant once no token is required.
notes: Author claims v0.0.43 rejects default installs with WS close 1006 and fixes it by making the hub tokenless unless an env var is set. Even if the 1006 symptom is real, the correct fix is to make token propagation reliable, not to default to no auth. Tests are rewritten to stub `CLINE_HUB_AUTH_TOKEN`, which hides the removal of the random-token guarantee. Should be closed or redirected.

title: Recognize progress in repeated tool-call loops
author: arafatkatze
blocking: 6 open review threads; large heuristic surface with no owner-defined contract for what counts as "progress"; only the known-flaky CLI TUI e2e case red
security_notes: This loosens a runtime safety guardrail: `LoopDetectionTracker` now resets the consecutive-identical-call counter whenever a repeated call's normalized output differs, so a model stuck in a loop against a tool with any output churn can run longer than before. The blast radius is bounded — failed outcomes never count as progress (`containsFailedToolOperation` also catches nested `{success:false}`), and a new absolute ceiling of `hardThreshold * 4` batches still aborts. The risk is heuristic quality, not malice: ~250 new lines of keyword sets (VOLATILE_OUTPUT_KEYS, LOG_OUTPUT_KEYS, PROGRESS_OUTPUT_KEYS) and regexes scrubbing timestamps/UUIDs out of arbitrary tool output.
notes: The loop-detection slice of #12465. The problem is real (identical polling calls with changing output currently abort a productive session) and the parallel-call correlation via `toolCallId` batches is thoughtfully done, with 62 tests. But it trades a simple deterministic abort rule for a large pile of string heuristics on top of a safety mechanism, which is a judgement call for the SDK owners.
